I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas, simp attributes or simp sets of its own. Every declaration is a private helper lemma or the final existential theorem. The long `attribute [-simp]` and `attribute [-instance]` lines only switch off other rules, and I found no sign they cause trouble here.

I looked at the small helper identities as possible canonical simp lemmas: `mem_restrictAlong_iff`, `ord_jQFun_eq`, `ord_jFun_eq` and `heckeBetaBar_jBar`. Their uses are all explicit `rw`s in one-off proofs, and I found no repeated use that a simp lemma would improve. `ord_jQFun_eq` and `ord_jFun_eq` unfold `ord` into a product with a ramification index. As simp lemmas they would unfold terms unconditionally and could clash with `Place.ord_restrictAlong`, so I would not recommend them.

The only `simp` calls are `simp [hz]`, `simp [hfa, hv]`, `simp [Ne.symm hfa]` and `simp [h0]`. They are local and closed by hypotheses, and I found no sign they are fragile or misdirected. I grepped for another `mem_restrictAlong_iff`. The one in Def_ModularCurve_CharLFrobeniusGeomLevel.lean is stated for an endomorphism `F →ₐ[K] F` and is a different declaration, so there is no competing simp rule.

I could not run Lean, so I did not check how the simplifier behaves in the proofs.
